title: Postern error response
description: Body of every non-2xx Postern response. See SPEC.md section 2.1. The root is closed: nothing may sit beside error, so this envelope has one extension point rather than two, and a client finds the whole failure under one key. That constrains what a conforming implementation emits — a client MUST NOT reject a response for carrying a sibling it does not recognise.

code.description: The codes a conforming implementation emits. A client MUST tolerate a code outside this set, treating it as a generic failure of its HTTP status class (SPEC.md section 2.1) — this enum is not a licence to reject. not_entitled is only valid from a local runner reporting its own state, and unauthorized only from a runner that requires inbound authentication of its own (SPEC.md section 7). Distributors MUST answer not_found instead of either, so the entitlement endpoint cannot be used to enumerate a private catalogue.

message.description: Human-readable; SHOULD be safe to show a user verbatim.

detail.description: Structured data about this failure, and the envelope's extension point: because the root is closed, whatever a bare code and message cannot carry rides here. Two members are defined so far: access_ends_at, the RFC 3339 date a withdrawn agent's access ends (SPEC.md section 5.6), and max_run_seconds, the duration bound a stopped run exceeded (section 4.5). Constraining those members is not the same as constraining detail: there is no required and no additionalProperties here, so an unrelated detail is unaffected and future members are still expected.

access_ends_at.description: SPEC.md section 5.6. The RFC 3339 date a withdrawn agent's access ends, so a client can say something true about it — which it cannot do with a string it has to guess the shape of.

max_run_seconds.description: SPEC.md section 4.5. Accompanies run_timeout: the declared duration bound the run exceeded, the same integer status reports as limits.max_run_seconds, so a client can name the limit that stopped it.
